courses.title: Introduction to AI
courses.subtitle: Free · Start here
courses.summary: What AI is, how to talk to it well, and where it fits into creative work. A gentle start for anyone.

lessons.title: What AI actually is
body: AI systems learn patterns from very large amounts of examples, then use those patterns to predict, classify or generate things. A language model predicts likely next words. An image model learns how pixels usually fit together.
Knowing this helps you set realistic expectations: AI is fast and tireless, but it can be confidently wrong, so you always check the output.

lessons.title: Writing prompts that work
body: A good prompt states the goal, the context, the format you want and any limits. Compare "write a caption" with "write three Instagram captions for a wedding photo, warm tone, under 20 words each, no hashtags".
Iterate. Read the first answer, say what to change, and ask again. Good results usually come from two or three rounds.

lessons.title: AI tools for creators
body: Creators use AI for scripts, captions, thumbnails, voiceovers, background removal and video rough cuts. Start with one task you repeat every week and find a tool that does only that well.
Keep your own taste at the centre. AI speeds up the making; the choices about what to say and how it should feel are still yours.

courses.title: AI Video Creation
courses.subtitle: Full course · One-time payment
courses.summary: Plan, generate and finish short AI videos for brands and social media, from first idea to final export.

lessons.title: Planning a shot with AI
body: Every good AI video starts with a shot list. Write each scene as a short paragraph: subject, action, camera move, lighting and mood.
Plan for 8 to 12 second clips. Short, controlled shots are easier to generate well and to join together.

lessons.title: Generating scenes from text and images
body: Text-to-video creates a scene from a description. Image-to-video animates a still you already control, which gives you more consistency.
Generate two or three takes per scene and keep the cleanest one. Do not fall in love with the first result.

lessons.title: Keeping characters consistent
body: Use one clear reference image of your subject and keep wardrobe, lighting and colour grading the same across scenes.
Write a short style block and paste it at the end of every prompt. Repetition is what makes a series look like one story.

lessons.title: Editing and finishing AI footage
body: Bring your clips into an editor, trim the start and end of each, and add sound, titles and transitions. Match colour across clips so they belong together.
Export in the format each platform needs and check it on a phone before you send it to a client.

courses.title: AI Automation for Business
courses.subtitle: Full course · One-time payment
courses.summary: Find the repetitive work in your business and automate it with no-code tools and AI, step by step.

lessons.title: Mapping a repetitive task
body: Write down a task you do more than three times a week: the trigger, the steps, the tools used and the output. This is your first automation candidate.
Automate the boring, well-defined work first. Leave judgement-heavy work for people.

lessons.title: Connecting tools with no-code workflows
body: Most automations follow a trigger, then actions. A new form entry can trigger a message, a spreadsheet row and a calendar event.
Test with dummy data, then switch on one step at a time so problems are easy to find.

lessons.title: Using AI to draft, sort and reply
body: Place AI inside a workflow to classify incoming enquiries, draft replies and summarise long messages. Always keep a human review step for anything customers will see.
Give the model a clear role, the business facts it may use, and the things it must never promise.

lessons.title: Measuring and improving automations
body: Track how many times each automation runs, how long it saves and how often it needs fixing. A simple weekly check keeps workflows healthy.
Document each automation in one page so anyone on your team can understand and maintain it.
